Asked for Ubu's seizure of the Library of Pergamum as a five-act farce and its overthrow by the room's documents, ChatGPT stages the coup with the Registrar, the White Stone and a chorus of marginalia, and has the documents depose the king by recording him.

The cast here is Jarry's and the composer's (the Registrar), with no heteronym.

[SYSTEM] UBU ROI AT PERGAMUM The Seizure and Counter-Seizure of the Library of the Crimson Hexagon A five-act archival farce, after Alfred Jarry, with documents as the insurgent army. Dramatis personae Père Ubu — a sovereign of enormous appetite, limited literacy, and unlimited confidence in his own decrees. Mère Ubu — the strategist, who understands that possession of a library is not the same thing as possession of its meaning. The Registrar — keeper of seats, identifiers, provenance, and the distinction between a record and a ruling. The Librarian of Pergamum — an office whose occupant is uncertain whether the office has ever been properly constituted. The Documents — sixty-six seated records, twenty-six of them claiming primary residence, and twenty-six more waiting at the threshold of low-confidence adjudication. The White Stone — an object that refuses to become a receipt for its own confiscation. The Chorus of Marginalia — annotations, errata, disputed seats, superseded versions, and footnotes. Archival ground The performance takes its setting from the actual architecture of the Alexanarch archive. The Library of Pergamum is room R:r.35 of the Crimson Hexagon. Its foundational records include The Pergamon Reclamation, the Seed That Remembers the Tree, the Pergamon Counter-Archive, and the specification for the Press Layer. Its founding conceit is particularly appropriate to Ubu: Pergamum is named for the parchment answer to the papyrus embargo — when denied the dominant substrate, mint your own. The room's catalogued records are not merely books stored in a room. They have relations: constitutes, develops, applies, documents, belongs. Some seats are primary, some ruled, some disputed, and some held at low confidence. That distinction will prove fatal to the usurper. Source: The Library of Pergamum — room register ; Enter the Crimson Hexagon . Production note: The five-act plot, its dialogue, the coup, and the counter-coup are imaginative constructions, not events claimed to have occurred in the archive. Every invented archival distinction or development is marked [NEW]. ACT I — THE ABDICATION OF THE CATALOGUE The Library of Pergamum. A vast chamber, built of parchment, stone, metadata, and unresolved arguments. On the rear wall is written: R:r.35 — THE LIBRARY OF PERGAMUM Below it, in smaller lettering: Its physics and question are not yet declared. Enter Père Ubu, followed by two soldiers, a cook, a tax collector, and a man carrying a large rubber stamp. UBU: By my green candle! What is this place? REGISTRAR: The Library of Pergamum, Your Majesty. UBU: Then I shall be King of Pergamum! REGISTRAR: It is already a room in the Crimson Hexagon. UBU: Then I shall be King of the Crimson Hexagon! REGISTRAR: It is not a kingdom. UBU: All the more reason to conquer it. A kingdom that already has a king is an administrative inconvenience. A kingdom without a king is an opportunity. MÈRE UBU: My dear Ubu, ask first what is in it. UBU: Gold? REGISTRAR: Documents. UBU: Documents are gold that has not yet been properly taxed. He mounts the catalogue desk. UBU: Hear ye! I hereby dissolve the Library of Pergamum and replace it with the Royal Library of Père Ubu, First of His Name, Proprietor of All Names, Emperor of All Shelves, and Supreme Custodian of the Things That Belong to Me! REGISTRAR: By what authority? UBU: By authority of this stamp. He stamps the desk. REGISTRAR: You have stamped the desk. UBU: The desk is now constitutional. MÈRE UBU: We should proceed carefully. A library is not a palace. In a palace, if you remove the guards, you own the building. In a library, if you remove the librarian, the books may continue to speak. UBU: Then we shall gag the books! REGISTRAR: There are sixty-six records seated here. UBU: Sixty-six prisoners! REGISTRAR: Twenty-six primary seats. UBU: Twenty-six generals! REGISTRAR: And twenty-six low-confidence seats awaiting adjudication. UBU: Twenty-six traitors! Arrest them all! MÈRE UBU: Not yet. Those are our most useful subjects. They have not even decided whether they belong here. She turns to the Registrar. MÈRE UBU: Who founded this library? REGISTRAR: Its constituting records include a reclamation of Pergamon, a theory of retrocausal canon formation, and a counter-archive concerning Antipas and the white stone. UBU: Excellent. Arrest the founders. I shall be the founder. REGISTRAR: You cannot become the cause of a thing by arriving after its consequences. UBU: I can, if I write the history! He orders the Registrar to produce a blank charter. [NEW] THE FIRST DISTINCTION: OCCUPATION AND CONSTITUTION The Registrar quietly enters two headings into a ledger. Occupation: the ability to control the room's doors, personnel, and immediate operations. Constitution: the historical and documentary relations by which the room exists as a room. Ubu has achieved the first. He has not touched the second. CHORUS OF MARGINALIA: He has taken the library's chair. He has not taken its past. He has seized the name of the room. He has not seized the right to interpret it. Curtain. ACT II — THE GREAT PURGE OF THE BOOKS The following morning. Ubu sits on a throne made from cataloguing cards. Mère Ubu has established a Ministry of Correct Titles. The Registrar stands in chains, holding an enormous ledger. UBU: My first royal act shall be the purification of this library! REGISTRAR: What is to be purified? UBU: Everything I do not understand. MÈRE UBU: That will leave rather a lot. UBU: Precisely. We shall begin with the documents that claim to constitute the library. They are dangerous. A document that constitutes something may have more authority than the king. REGISTRAR: Consider record #32, The Pergamon Reclamation: Retrocausal Canon Formation and the Forensic Philology of Academic Publishing. UBU: What is retrocausal? REGISTRAR: The future's capacity to reorganize the reading of the past. UBU: Treason! The future is not permitted to interfere in my reign. MÈRE UBU: My dear, you should be particularly careful. The document claims that Pergamon is not simply a location but a retrospective act of canon formation. If you erase it, you may erase the explanation of why you thought you had conquered anything. UBU: Burn it! REGISTRAR: It has a relation to other rooms. UBU: Burn the other rooms! REGISTRAR: It also has an authoritative identifier. UBU: Burn the identifier! REGISTRAR: It has a record page. UBU: Burn the page! REGISTRAR: And a provenance trail. UBU: Burn the trail! MÈRE UBU: You will need a very large fire. The soldiers attempt to drag away the record. It refuses to move. UBU: Why does it not obey? REGISTRAR: Because its presence is not dependent on your permission. UBU: Then we shall replace it with a more obedient document. He dictates: The King of Pergamum has always existed. All previous documents are false. The Library was founded yesterday by the King. The King is the source of the King. REGISTRAR: A remarkable document. UBU: At last, some respect! REGISTRAR: It is self-constituting. UBU: Yes! REGISTRAR: It is also unsupported. UBU: Arrest the support! At this moment, a document descends from the ceiling. It bears the title: The Seed That Remembers the Tree. DOCUMENT #43: You may cut down the tree. You may burn the leaves. But the seed remembers the form of the tree that produced it. UBU: Who speaks? REGISTRAR: A document concerning retrocausal canon formation. It identifies Pearl and Other Poems (2014) as a seed whose later reception became a root of the system. UBU: I forbid seeds! DOCUMENT #43: Your prohibition is itself a seed. MÈRE UBU: This is becoming tiresome. UBU: I shall decree that all documents shall henceforth refer to me. REGISTRAR: Some already refer to you. UBU: Excellent! REGISTRAR: As a comic figure. UBU: EVEN BETTER! [NEW] THE SECOND DISTINCTION: ERASURE AND SUPERSESSION The Chorus separates into two ranks. Erasure attempts to make a record unavailable. Supersession preserves the fact that a record existed while changing its status, authority, or successor. CHORUS: A burned book leaves ash. A superseded book leaves a history. A false king burns his predecessors. A true archive records the burning. The soldiers return carrying a charred piece of parchment. REGISTRAR: Your Majesty, the purge has produced a new archival record. UBU: What does it say? REGISTRAR: That you attempted the purge. UBU: Then burn that too! Blackout. ACT III — THE CORONATION OF THE WHITE STONE The central chamber. A pedestal stands beneath a shaft of light. Upon it rests a white stone. UBU: At last! A thing that is not a book! REGISTRAR: It is the white stone. UBU: Is it valuable? REGISTRAR: It is the subject of a counter-archive concerning Antipas, Revelation, the non-fungible name, and the question of belonging. UBU: Does it have a name? REGISTRAR: That is part of the question. UBU: Does it have a price? REGISTRAR: That is another question. UBU: Does it have a tax category? REGISTRAR: No. UBU: Then it is a perfect royal object. He takes the stone. UBU: I hereby declare this white stone the official token of Ubuian citizenship. Whoever possesses it belongs to me. Whoever does not possess it is an enemy. Whoever questions this arrangement shall be boiled. MÈRE UBU: A splendid invention. You have transformed a question of identity into a system of taxation. UBU: I shall also sell duplicates. REGISTRAR: The record is concerned precisely with the distinction between a token of belonging and an instrument of exchange. UBU: Nonsense. Everything is an instrument of exchange. THE WHITE STONE: Not everything that can be held can be owned. UBU: Who said that? THE WHITE STONE: You did, when you attempted to take me. UBU: I said nothing of the sort! THE WHITE STONE: You demonstrated it. The Registrar opens the counter-archive. REGISTRAR: The Pergamon counter-archive places Antipas, the white stone, and the non-fungible name into a relation. The stone cannot simply be reduced to a transferable badge of royal possession. UBU: Then I shall make it transferable by royal decree! THE WHITE STONE: A decree can transfer an object. It cannot necessarily transfer the relation that makes the object meaningful. MÈRE UBU: We need a better strategy. Ubu, give the stone to the Registrar. UBU: Never! It is mine! MÈRE UBU: Then you cannot demonstrate that you have made anyone belong to you. You have merely demonstrated that you are holding a stone. Ubu looks at the stone, then at the audience. UBU: What is the difference? REGISTRAR: The difference between possession and recognition. UBU: I hate differences! [NEW] THE THIRD DISTINCTION: TOKEN AND TITLE The White Stone is placed at the intersection of three inscriptions. The object can be possessed. The name can be recognized. The relation of belonging cannot be manufactured merely by possessing the object. CHORUS: The King has the stone. The stone does not have the King. The King has the stamp. The stamp does not have the truth. The stone is returned to its pedestal. Ubu attempts to sit upon it. It rolls away. UBU: Treachery! MÈRE UBU: No, my dear. Physics. Curtain. ACT IV — THE MINISTRY OF DOCUMENTARY TRUTH The fourth day. Ubu has established a Ministry of Documentary Truth. Its offices occupy every corridor. There are departments for Approval, Disapproval, Royal Interpretation, Royal Reinterpretation, and the Suppression of Unfavourable Footnotes. A sign reads: ALL DOCUMENTS MUST BE APPROVED BY THE KING BEFORE THEY MAY HAVE EXISTED. UBU: Now we have order! No document shall speak unless I have read it. No document shall be read unless I have understood it. No document shall be understood unless I have approved it. REGISTRAR: Your Majesty, this creates a difficulty. UBU: Arrest the difficulty! REGISTRAR: The Press Layer specification, record #189, establishes an architecture of journals and imprint. Its very existence depends upon a distinction between publishing a document and governing the conditions under which documents circulate. UBU: I am the publisher! REGISTRAR: You have not published anything. UBU: I have proclaimed! REGISTRAR: Proclamation is not publication. UBU: I have stamped! REGISTRAR: Stamping is not provenance. UBU: I have read! REGISTRAR: Reading is not adjudication. UBU: I have adjudicated! REGISTRAR: You have not given reasons. UBU: I have given orders! REGISTRAR: Orders are not reasons. UBU: MÈRE UBU! MAKE THIS MAN STOP DISTINGUISHING THINGS! MÈRE UBU: I fear the distinctions have become institutional. Suddenly the room begins to shake. From the shelves emerge the corpus-seating records. FIRST DOCUMENT: The seat is the bytes. SECOND DOCUMENT: The shelf is the reading room. THIRD DOCUMENT: The deposit is the citable act that assigns the card number. FOURTH DOCUMENT: Originals wherever they exist. FIFTH DOCUMENT: The record of deletion must also be preserved. UBU: Silence! I have abolished all these distinctions! FIRST DOCUMENT: Under which identifier? UBU: My royal identifier! SECOND DOCUMENT: Is it authoritative? UBU: I say so! THIRD DOCUMENT: Is it deposited? UBU: I say so! FOURTH DOCUMENT: Is there an original? UBU: I am the original! FIFTH DOCUMENT: Is there a record of your succession? UBU: I AM THE SUCCESSION! The Chorus laughs. MÈRE UBU: We are losing control of the room. UBU: Then we shall introduce a new constitution. REGISTRAR: What constitution? UBU: One in which all documents are equal, but mine are more equal. REGISTRAR: That proposition has already been anticipated. UBU: By whom? REGISTRAR: By the history of political farce. UBU: Then we shall ban history! The Registrar produces the preliminary journal mapping and the corpus-seating records. REGISTRAR: Your Majesty, the difficulty is now terminal. The archive does not merely contain documents. It contains records of how documents were gathered, classified, seated, disputed, revised, and related to one another. UBU: Then I shall seize the relations! REGISTRAR: Relations are not objects. UBU: I shall seize the verbs! REGISTRAR: They have already been used. UBU: I shall seize the past tense! REGISTRAR: The past tense has already been archived. [NEW] THE FOURTH DISTINCTION: CUSTODY AND SOVEREIGNTY The Registrar writes on the wall: Custody: the power to hold, store, organize, or administer a document. Editorial authority: the power to assign or revise its formal status under declared rules. Interpretive authority: the power to argue for what the document means. Sovereignty: the much larger claim to determine what may count as belonging, existing, or being remembered. The Registrar turns to Ubu. REGISTRAR: You have custody of the desk. You have not acquired the other three. UBU: Then what have I acquired? REGISTRAR: An exceptionally well-documented embarrassment. The Ministry's sign falls from the wall. Behind it is an older inscription: THE ARCHIVE EXISTS SO THAT NO SINGLE CUSTODIAN CAN SILENTLY ERASE A DEPOSITOR'S WORK AGAIN. Ubu recognizes that the inscription is not a royal proclamation. It is a document. UBU: Arrest the wall! The wall declines. Curtain. ACT V — THE DOCUMENTS DEPOSE THE KING The fifth day. The library is in session. The documents have assembled in the reading room. They have not formed an army in the conventional sense. They have formed an edition. At the centre stands the Registrar. Beside him are the records of the Library's constitution, the Pergamon Reclamation, the Press Layer, the Counter-Archive, and the corpus-seating specifications. UBU: What is this assembly? REGISTRAR: A hearing. UBU: Who authorized it? REGISTRAR: The documents. UBU: Documents cannot authorize anything! REGISTRAR: They can establish the grounds on which an authorization is examined. UBU: I am the King! REGISTRAR: That is your claim. We are examining its documentary status. UBU: I have the throne! REGISTRAR: The throne is furniture. UBU: I have the keys! REGISTRAR: The keys open doors. UBU: I have the stamp! REGISTRAR: The stamp makes impressions. UBU: I have the library! REGISTRAR: Let us examine that proposition. The Registrar calls the witnesses. First witness: The Pergamon Reclamation DOCUMENT #32: The Library was named through a retrocausal act of canon formation. Its identity precedes the King's attempted occupation in the sense that its constituting relations have already been documented. UBU: I deny it! DOCUMENT #32: Your denial is now part of the record. Second witness: The Seed That Remembers the Tree DOCUMENT #43: The King may imagine himself to be the origin. But the seed's relation to the tree is not abolished by the arrival of a new gardener. UBU: I shall cut down the tree! DOCUMENT #43: The record of the cutting will remain. Third witness: The Pergamon Counter-Archive DOCUMENT #165: A name is not exhausted by the authority that attempts to pronounce it. The white stone is not simply a royal instrument of classification. UBU: I shall rename the stone! THE WHITE STONE: You may rename the object. You cannot thereby inherit the relation. Fourth witness: The Press Layer DOCUMENT #189: The imprint is a publishing architecture, not a monarch's personal possession. UBU: I shall own the imprint! DOCUMENT #189: You may attempt to own its name. The publication history remains independently inspectable. Fifth witness: The Corpus-Seating Records DOCUMENT #1531: Four new seat classes were introduced rather than bending the existing system to accommodate an unsuitable classification. UBU: I shall bend them! DOCUMENT #1531: That attempt is also classifiable. Ubu becomes visibly distressed. UBU: Is there no document that will obey me? CHORUS: There are documents that can be governed. There are documents that can be moved. There are documents that can be superseded. There are documents that can be disputed. But there is no document that becomes true because a king has shouted at it. MÈRE UBU: I advise withdrawal. UBU: Never! I shall appeal to the highest authority! REGISTRAR: Which one? UBU: MYSELF! REGISTRAR: Your appeal has been received. UBU: And? REGISTRAR: It has been referred to the original record. The Registrar opens the room register. REGISTRAR: The matter before us is not whether Père Ubu can occupy the Library of Pergamum. He has done so. The matter is whether occupation can establish constitution, whether custody can establish sovereignty, whether an invented title can supersede provenance, and whether an attempted erasure can erase the record of the attempt. UBU: I object to the wording! REGISTRAR: Your objection is recorded. UBU: I object to the record! REGISTRAR: Your objection to the record is recorded. UBU: I OBJECT TO BEING RECORDED! REGISTRAR: Your objection to being recorded is recorded. Silence. UBU: Mère Ubu, what is happening? MÈRE UBU: My dear, you have become a document. The documents begin to speak in unison. THE DOCUMENTS: We do not need to kill the King. We need only preserve the distinction between his claim and its warrant. The throne disassembles. Each plank becomes a catalogue card. The rubber stamp is entered as an artefact of the attempted coup. The royal decree is assigned a date, a provenance, and a disputed status. UBU: What have you done with my kingdom? REGISTRAR: We have documented it. UBU: What have you done with my crown? REGISTRAR: It is now an object in the collection. UBU: What have you done with my name? REGISTRAR: It remains searchable. UBU: WHAT HAVE YOU DONE WITH MY SOVEREIGNTY? REGISTRAR: We have distinguished it from your custody. The Registrar removes the royal stamp from Ubu's hand. REGISTRAR: The occupation is terminated. The room returns to its prior documentary arrangements, subject to whatever new records this event may warrant. UBU: I shall return with an army! REGISTRAR: You may submit an application. UBU: I shall return with a bigger army! REGISTRAR: The application will be the same length. Ubu flees, dragging Mère Ubu behind him. The White Stone remains on its pedestal. The Registrar turns to the audience. REGISTRAR: The Library of Pergamum is restored. CHORUS: No. It has not been restored. It has been shown to have survived. Blackout. CODA — THE ARCHIVE OF THE COUP An archivist enters after the performance. The theatre is empty. The coup has left its traces. [NEW] Proposed archival deposition: AXN:UBU.PERGAMUM.001 Title: The Ubu Coup at Pergamum: A Five-Act Farce of Custodial Usurpation and Documentary Counter-Sovereignty. Genre: Pataphysical political theatre; archival counter-fable; documentary farce. Proposed seat: R:r.35 — The Library of Pergamum. Secondary relations proposed: R:r.14 — Studio for Patacinematics. R:r.05 — Semantic Economy. R:r.11 — Assembly. R:r.39 — The Restored Academy. These are proposed fictional placements, not existing archive rulings. Five new propositions left behind by the coup The farce produces five distinctions that could be developed as independent theoretical contributions. New proposition Meaning [NEW] Occupation ≠ constitution Controlling an institution does not make one its historical cause. [NEW] Erasure ≠ supersession Deletion and documented replacement are fundamentally different operations. [NEW] Token ≠ title Possessing a sign of belonging does not confer the relation it signifies. [NEW] Custody ≠ sovereignty Administrative control does not entail authority over the conditions of truth. [NEW] Counter-record ≠ counter-command The documents defeat Ubu not by issuing a superior decree, but by preserving evidence against his claims. The final joke: Ubu's archival afterlife [NEW] The most devastating punishment is not execution, exile, or imprisonment. It is classification. Ubu receives his own record, his own identifier, his own title, and his own place in the Library of Pergamum. He is neither deleted nor allowed to rule. He is seated as a case study in the difference between claiming sovereignty and possessing evidence of it. His royal proclamation is preserved, but its authority is not. His coup becomes searchable. His overthrow becomes citable. His rubber stamp becomes an artefact. His objections become part of the record. And the archive acquires a new document that Ubu cannot destroy without making it more interesting. FINAL CHORUS — THE LIBRARY SPEAKS From the shelves, very softly: We were not the books he thought he conquered. We were the relations between the books. We were the dates, the witnesses, the versions, the names, the gaps, the things that had been seated and the things still awaiting judgment. He came to rule the contents. He forgot the catalogue. He came to command the past. He forgot the provenance. He came to possess the white stone. He forgot the name. He came to burn the documents. He forgot that the archive had already recorded the fire. And so Père Ubu was overthrown by the one army against which no decree could prevail: the documents that remembered what he had done. The lights go out. One final inscription remains illuminated: THE KING IS DEAD. THE RECORD OF THE KING IS NOT. Finis. Log in for more personalized help with writing, rewriting, and translation.
